title: frozen-comparand lint has no quote awareness: it flags `-eq N` inside quoted test-input strings and grep search patterns, making it impossible to author behavioral oracles for the rule itself
description:
MEASURED LIVE, and it deterministically blocked a real plan twice, escalating it.

While planning CAM-382 (widening the frozen-comparand rule), the deterministic oracle lint at src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:1036 blocked BOTH re-plan rounds and wrote .claude/.cam-plan-escalated.json with roundsCompleted:2. All THREE findings are FALSE POSITIVES. Verbatim from the escalation marker:

  1. bun -e 'const {RULES}=await import("./src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts");const r=RULES.find(x=>x.name==="frozen-comparand");const cs=["test $X -eq 41","test $X -ge 41","test $X -le 41","test $X == 41"];for(const c of cs){if(r.test(c)===null){...}}'
  2. bun -e '...const cs=["cmd --ge 5","echo foo-eq 42"];for(const c of cs){if(r.test(c)!==null){...}}'
  3. grep -qF 'test $(git grep -c PATTERN mainbranch:file.ts) -eq 1' test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts

In (1) and (2) the `-eq 41` / `--ge 5` are TEST INPUT DATA inside a quoted JS array, passed to rule.test() by a behavioral oracle. In (3) the `-eq 1` is the SEARCH PATTERN of a grep -qF, i.e. the literal text being looked for in a test file. None of the three is a shell comparison at all.

ROOT CAUSE: hasFrozenIntegerComparand (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:168-171) applies INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE to the WHOLE command string as a flat regex. It has no notion of shell quoting, no tokenization, and no awareness that a match may sit inside a single-quoted, double-quoted, or nested string literal. Any occurrence of the operator+integer byte pattern anywhere in the command trips it.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A GENERIC FALSE POSITIVE: it is SELF-REFERENTIAL. The natural way to write a falsifiable acceptance oracle for a rule that classifies shell comparisons is to feed it example shell comparisons and assert the classification. That oracle necessarily embeds comparison-shaped strings as data. So the rule structurally forbids behavioral oracles about itself, which is exactly the oracle style patterns.md and the project convention otherwise push authors toward. Any future story touching this rule hits the same wall.

It also false-positives well beyond this module: ANY oracle that greps for text containing a comparison (`grep -qF 'test ... -eq 1' somefile`) is flagged, which is a common and legitimate way to pin that a test file contains a specific assertion.

DIRECTION (needs a real decision, do not headless-implement): make the scan quote-aware, so a match inside a quoted string literal is not treated as a live comparison. Options worth weighing: strip or skip single/double-quoted spans before scanning; require the comparison to sit in shell command position; or add an explicit authoring escape hatch. Note that stripping quoted spans would also weaken genuine detection for oracles that legitimately quote their whole test expression, so this is a real trade-off, not a one-liner. Whatever is chosen must keep the rule catching the CAM-377 shape it exists for.

RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER ISSUES: CAM-383 is the OPPOSITE error (over-EXCUSING: any derivation token anywhere excuses every comparand). This is over-FLAGGING. CAM-382 (widening the operator alternation to -gt/-lt/-ne/!=) will make this STRICTLY WORSE, since more operators means more byte patterns that can appear inside quoted data. CAM-386 is a third axis (what counts as a derivation token). All four live in the same ~30 lines. Sequencing matters: shipping CAM-382 without this fix makes the self-referential trap harder to escape.

BLAST RADIUS TODAY: this is not theoretical. It cost a full plan phase plus two re-plan rounds and left .claude/.cam-plan-escalated.json on disk. The lint runs BEFORE the auditor is ever spawned, so a false positive here burns the whole planning cycle with no auditor judgment applied.

Needs rebuild: prd-oracle-lint.ts is sidecar-executed at plan time.
